subject.title: fix: prevent operational notices from leaking to source chats

question: Should OpenClaw accept `messages.operationalReplies` as a core operator-controlled security and delivery contract, including fail-closed redirect behavior and the new plugin-hook/session-state surfaces?
rationale: The PR intentionally controls disclosure and redirection of provider errors, fallback state, usage limits, status details, and other operational information; automation cannot decide whether this public policy and its failure semantics match the repository's product and trust model.

options.title: Approve after live proof
options.body: Accept the centralized policy after exact-head checks pass and redacted real-channel evidence proves default, silent, once, redirect, restart, and redirect-failure behavior.

options.title: Split the policy surface
options.body: Land narrower notice-classification or leak fixes first and defer redirect, once-state, and plugin-hook contracts to a separately approved design.

options.title: Reject the core setting
options.body: Keep operational-notice behavior fixed in core or owner-specific paths rather than adding a permanent operator-facing routing policy.

recommendation.title: Approve after live proof
recommendation.body: Accept the centralized policy after exact-head checks pass and redacted real-channel evidence proves default, silent, once, redirect, restart, and redirect-failure behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses core reply delivery, config compatibility, plugin API shape, persistent session state, and security-sensitive routing, matching this person's broad adjacent history.
